style_note: Soft 3D animated film look. Camera almost still with only a slight drift, keep full framing, no cuts inside a shot, no text, no logos. Characters keep their faces and outfits.

voices.narrator: warm, thoughtful man in his thirties, calm British-neutral English, close-mic, like telling a friend a true story
voices.giulia: young woman about 30, bright, warm, slightly teasing
voices.mum: woman in her 50s, gentle, a little worried then relieved
voices.dad: man in his 50s, warm, low voice

shots.motion: The father and daughter laugh and pile more food onto their plates, a hand passes another pizza across the table. The Shiba's eyes follow each plate as it moves, unimpressed.
shots.caption: We loved dinner.

shots.motion: The family sink deeper into the sofa, the father puffs out his cheeks, the mother rubs her stomach, the daughter groans. The Shiba lets out a slow sigh and lowers its chin onto its paws.
shots.caption: Our bodies didn't.

shots.motion: Calm, happy dinner with balanced plates. The daughter serves herself a sensible portion, laughs and says her line. The Shiba gives a small satisfied nod.
shots.caption: Same table. Just the right amount.

shots.motion: Giulia flexes in the mirror, looks closer, frowns and lets her arm drop. The Shiba on the gym bag tilts its head.
shots.caption: Six months. Same arms.

shots.motion: Giulia eats a cracker standing in the fridge light, tired, scrolling her phone. The Shiba in the doorway watches and blinks slowly.

dialogue.giulia: I train like an athlete. I eat like I forgot.

shots.motion: Giulia completes a strong, controlled curl with a small proud smile. The Shiba watches approvingly, tail swishing.

voiceover.giulia: Now it knows what I lifted and what I ate. Finally, it adds up.

shots.motion: Luca, exhausted, straightens up slowly and lunges for a ball too late, it bounces past him. The Shiba behind the fence winces.
shots.caption: Third set. Nothing left.

shots.motion: Luca gulps from the can and bites the pastry in a hurry, checks the time. The Shiba in the back seat stares at the pastry, then at him.
shots.caption: Lunch, apparently.

shots.motion: Luca celebrates the winning shot, grinning, and points his racket at the Shiba, who wags its tail.

dialogue.luca: Turns out the problem wasn't my backhand.

shots.motion: The mother lowers the letter, worried; the father puts a hand on her shoulder. The Shiba looks up at them softly.

dialogue.mum: Cholesterol again. What are we supposed to eat?

shots.motion: The parents cook together, the father tastes from the spoon and nods, surprised it is good; the mother smiles at the phone. The Shiba sniffs the air.
The parents walk briskly through the sunny park laughing, the Shiba trotting ahead on the lead.

voiceover.mum: We're not dieting. We just finally know what our results mean on a plate.

shots.caption: Prevention is better than cure.

shots.motion: Very slow push-in towards the house at dusk; the Shiba at the window turns its head towards the family.

voiceover.narrator: I'm in my thirties. I play too many sports. And somewhere after thirty, I learned that muscle doesn't stay on its own.
I trained hard. But what I ate was guesswork. Everyone guesses. And almost everyone guesses wrong.
We weren't unhealthy people. We just never connected what was on the plate with how we felt the next day.
Then my parents got their blood results. Numbers on a page. Nobody told them which foods those numbers were about.

shots.motion: Luca types, stops, rubs his eyes and sighs at the long message. The Shiba on the bed opens one eye.

voiceover.narrator: I tried asking an AI. Every single morning I explained my life again, from zero. As if yesterday never happened.

shots.motion: The Shiba's eyes follow a fork from plate to mouth, then it gives a small knowing tilt of the head.

voiceover.narrator: So I built a coach that remembers. It knows what you ate, how you trained and what your bloods say, and it connects the dots nobody connects.
We called him Zabaione. He notices everything. He never judges. He just helps you get it a little more right, every day.

shots.motion: The family walk slowly into the sunset, the Shiba looks back at them and trots on.

voiceover.narrator: Because the best time to look after your health is before you have to.
